key_insight: A GPT-2 table-to-text framework can outperform traditional ML and neural networks on small, imbalanced clinical datasets by turning structured records into clinically meaningful text for prediction.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help improve early disease risk prediction from low-volume hospital data while keeping the output more interpretable for clinicians.
method: Converted structured clinical variables into physician-style text.
Used GPT-4 paraphrasing to augment minority-class examples while preserving medical meaning.
Fine-tuned GPT-2 on four public datasets and applied gradient-based explainability to identify important features.
evidence_signal: Across heart disease, heart failure, chronic kidney disease, and thyroid cancer recurrence datasets, the model reported average precision, specificity, sensitivity, and F1-score of 0.96, 0.97, 0.96, and 0.96.
watch_item: Results come from public benchmark datasets, so performance and clinical utility may differ in real-world settings with noisier data, different prevalence, or site-specific biases.
paper_title: Can GPT Be Used as an Alternative Prediction Model to Traditional Machine Learning and Neural Networks on Low-Volume Clinical Data?
